questions.question: Why are spaces mandatory around the '+' and '-' operators in the CSS calc() function?
options: To make the stylesheet load faster
Because without spaces, the minus sign is parsed as a negative number or hyphenated identifier
It is only required on Linux servers
Spaces are optional in all modern browsers
questions.hint: Syntax ambiguity between subtraction and negative numbers.
questions.explanation: In calc(), '+' and '-' must have whitespace on both sides so the parser differentiates operators from negative numbers.

questions.question: What are the three arguments passed into the clamp() function in order?
options: (maximum, minimum, preferred)
(minimum, preferred, maximum)
(start, center, end)
(factor, scale, threshold)
questions.explanation: clamp() takes three parameters: minimum acceptable value, preferred dynamic calculation, and maximum bound.

questions.question: Which function ensures an element's width never exceeds 800px while taking 100% of the screen on smaller devices?
options: width: min(100%, 800px);
width: max(100%, 800px);
width: calc(100% * 800px);
width: clamp(800px);
questions.hint: min() picks whichever value is smaller.
questions.explanation: width: min(100%, 800px) chooses 100% on small screens and caps at 800px on wide screens.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of 'Fluid Typography' implemented with clamp()?
options: It makes fonts change colors automatically
It smoothly scales font size continuously with viewport width without abrupt media query jumps
It allows using non-web fonts without downloading
It animates font weights continuously
questions.hint: Continuous smooth scaling without media query breakpoints.
questions.explanation: Fluid typography with clamp() continuously scales text size with the screen width, avoiding jarring breakpoint jumps.

questions.question: Can you perform calculations mixing different units (such as percentages and pixels) inside calc()?
options: No, units must all be pixels
Yes, calc() can mix percentages, rems, viewport units, and pixels seamlessly
Only in Sass, not in pure CSS
Only with multiplication
questions.explanation: calc() is designed to mix disparate units at runtime (e.g. calc(100% - 32px)).
